verses.original: וַיְהִ֨י מִיָּמִ֜ים בִּימֵ֣י קְצִיר־ חִטִּ֗ים וַיִּפְקֹ֨ד שִׁמְשׁ֤וֹן אֶת־ אִשְׁתּוֹ֙ בִּגְדִ֣י עִזִּ֔ים וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אָבֹ֥אָה אֶל־ אִשְׁתִּ֖י הֶחָ֑דְרָה וְלֹֽא־ נְתָנ֥וֹ אָבִ֖יהָ לָבֽוֹא׃
verses.transliteration: way·hî mî·yā·mîm bî·mê qə·ṣîr- ḥiṭ·ṭîm way·yip̄·qōḏ šim·šō·wn ’eṯ- ’iš·tōw biḡ·ḏî ‘iz·zîm way·yō·mer ’ā·ḇō·’āh ’el- ’iš·tî he·ḥā·ḏə·rāh wə·lō- nə·ṯā·nōw ’ā·ḇî·hā lā·ḇō·w
verses.literal: Later on . . . at the time of the wheat harvest Samson took a young goat and went to visit his wife I want to go to my wife in her room he said But her father would not let him enter
verses.literalPt: E ACONTECEU, depois de alguns dias, que, na sega do trigo, Sansão visitou a sua mulher, com um cabrito, e disse: Entrarei na câmara de minha mulher. Porém o pai dela não o deixou entrar.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אָבִ֗יהָ אָמֹ֤ר אָמַ֙רְתִּי֙ כִּי־ שָׂנֹ֣א שְׂנֵאתָ֔הּ וָאֶתְּנֶ֖נָּה לְמֵרֵעֶ֑ךָ הֲלֹ֨א אֲחֹתָ֤הּ הַקְּטַנָּה֙ טוֹבָ֣ה מִמֶּ֔נָּה תְּהִי־ נָ֥א לְךָ֖ תַּחְתֶּֽיהָ׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ’ā·ḇî·hā ’ā·mōr ’ā·mar·tî kî- śā·nō śə·nê·ṯāh wā·’et·tə·nen·nāh lə·mê·rê·‘e·ḵā hă·lō ’ă·ḥō·ṯāh haq·qə·ṭan·nāh ṭō·w·ḇāh mim·men·nāh tə·hî- nā lə·ḵā taḥ·te·hā
verses.literal: I was sure . . . that you thoroughly hated her . . . said her father so I gave her to one of the men who accompanied you Is not her younger sister more beautiful than she Please take her instead
verses.literalPt: E disse-lhe seu pai: Por certo pensava eu que de todo a desprezavas; de sorte que a dei ao teu companheiro; porém não é sua irmã mais nova, mais formosa do que ela? Toma-a, pois, em seu lugar.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ שִׁמְשׁ֔וֹן נִקֵּ֥יתִי הַפַּ֖עַם מִפְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים כִּֽי־ עֹשֶׂ֥ה אֲנִ֛י עִמָּ֖ם רָעָֽה׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer lā·hem šim·šō·wn niq·qê·ṯî hap·pa·‘am mip·pə·liš·tîm kî- ‘ō·śeh ’ă·nî ‘im·mām rā·‘āh
verses.literal: Samson said to them This time I will be blameless - in doing harm to the Philistines
verses.literalPt: Então Sansão disse acerca deles: Inocente sou esta vez para com os filisteus, quando lhes fizer algum mal.

verses.original: וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ שִׁמְשׁ֔וֹן וַיִּלְכֹּ֖ד שְׁלֹשׁ־ מֵא֣וֹת שׁוּעָלִ֑ים וַיִּקַּ֣ח לַפִּדִ֗ים וַיֶּ֤פֶן זָנָב֙ אֶל־ זָנָ֔ב וַיָּ֨שֶׂם לַפִּ֥יד אֶחָ֛ד בֵּין־ שְׁנֵ֥י הַזְּנָב֖וֹת בַּתָּֽוֶךְ׃
verses.transliteration: way·yê·leḵ šim·šō·wn way·yil·kōḏ šə·lōš- mê·’ō·wṯ šū·‘ā·lîm way·yiq·qaḥ lap·pi·ḏîm way·ye·p̄en zā·nāḇ ’el- zā·nāḇ way·yā·śem lap·pîḏ ’e·ḥāḏ bên- šə·nê haz·zə·nā·ḇō·wṯ bat·tā·weḵ
verses.literal: Then Samson went out and caught three hundred foxes And he took torches turned the foxes tail-to-tail . . . . . . and fastened a torch between each pair of tails . . .
verses.literalPt: E foi Sansão, e pegou trezentas raposas; e, tomando tochas, as virou cauda a cauda, e lhes pôs uma tocha no meio de cada duas caudas.

verses.original: וַיַּבְעֶר־ אֵשׁ֙ בַּלַּפִּידִ֔ים וַיְשַׁלַּ֖ח בְּקָמ֣וֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַיַּבְעֵ֛ר מִגָּדִ֥ישׁ וְעַד־ קָמָ֖ה וְעַד־ כֶּ֥רֶם זָֽיִת׃
verses.transliteration: way·yaḇ·‘er- ’êš bal·lap·pî·ḏîm way·šal·laḥ bə·qā·mō·wṯ pə·liš·tîm way·yaḇ·‘êr mig·gā·ḏîš wə·‘aḏ- qā·māh wə·‘aḏ- ke·rem zā·yiṯ
verses.literal: Then he lit . . . the torches and released the foxes into the standing grain of the Philistines burning up the piles of grain . . . and the standing grain as well as the vineyards and olive groves
verses.literalPt: E chegou fogo às tochas, e largou-as na seara dos filisteus; e assim abrasou os molhos com a sega do trigo, e as vinhas e os olivais.

verses.original: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ פְלִשְׁתִּים֮ מִ֣י עָ֣שָׂה זֹאת֒ וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ שִׁמְשׁוֹן֙ חֲתַ֣ן הַתִּמְנִ֔י כִּ֚י לָקַ֣ח אֶת־ אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ וַֽיִּתְּנָ֖הּ לְמֵרֵעֵ֑הוּ וַיַּעֲל֣וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וַיִּשְׂרְפ֥וּ אוֹתָ֛הּ וְאֶת־ אָבִ֖יהָ בָּאֵֽשׁ׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mə·rū p̄ə·liš·tîm mî ‘ā·śāh zōṯ way·yō·mə·rū šim·šō·wn ḥă·ṯan hat·tim·nî kî lā·qaḥ ’eṯ- ’iš·tōw way·yit·tə·nāh lə·mê·rê·‘ê·hū way·ya·‘ă·lū p̄ə·liš·tîm way·yiś·rə·p̄ū ’ō·w·ṯāh wə·’eṯ- ’ā·ḇî·hā bā·’êš
verses.literal: Who did this the Philistines demanded It was Samson the son-in-law of the Timnite they were told For - his wife was given to his companion So the Philistines went up and burned her and her father - to death
verses.literalPt: Então perguntaram os filisteus: Quem fez isto? E responderam: Sansão, o genro do timnita, porque lhe tomou a sua mulher, e a deu a seu companheiro. Então subiram os filisteus, e queimaram a fogo a ela e a seu pai.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ שִׁמְשׁ֔וֹן אִֽם־ תַּעֲשׂ֖וּן כָּזֹ֑את כִּ֛י אִם־ נִקַּ֥מְתִּי בָכֶ֖ם וְאַחַ֥ר אֶחְדָּֽל׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer lā·hem šim·šō·wn ’im- ta·‘ă·śūn kā·zōṯ kî ’im- niq·qam·tî ḇā·ḵem wə·’a·ḥar ’eḥ·dāl
verses.literal: And Samson told them Because you have done this I will not rest until . . . I have taken vengeance upon you
verses.literalPt: Então lhes disse Sansão: É assim que fazeis? Pois, havendo-me vingado eu de vós, então cessarei.

verses.original: וַיַּ֨ךְ אוֹתָ֥ם שׁ֛וֹק עַל־ יָרֵ֖ךְ מַכָּ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֑ה וַיֵּ֣רֶד וַיֵּ֔שֶׁב בִּסְעִ֖יף סֶ֥לַע עֵיטָֽם׃ס
verses.transliteration: way·yaḵ ’ō·w·ṯām šō·wq ‘al- yā·rêḵ mak·kāh ḡə·ḏō·w·lāh way·yê·reḏ way·yê·šeḇ bis·‘îp̄ se·la‘ ‘ê·ṭām
verses.literal: And he struck them ruthlessly . . . . . . with a great slaughter and then went down and stayed in the cave at the rock of Etam
verses.literalPt: E feriu-os com grande ferimento, pernas juntamente com coxa; e desceu, e habitou na fenda da rocha de Etã.

verses.original: וַיַּעֲל֣וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בִּיהוּדָ֑ה וַיִּנָּטְשׁ֖וּ בַּלֶּֽחִי׃
verses.transliteration: way·ya·‘ă·lū p̄ə·liš·tîm way·ya·ḥă·nū bî·hū·ḏāh way·yin·nā·ṭə·šū bal·le·ḥî
verses.literal: Then the Philistines went up camped in Judah and deployed themselves near the town of Lehi
verses.literalPt: Então os filisteus subiram, e acamparam-se contra Judá, e estenderam-se por Leí.

verses.original: וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדָ֔ה לָמָ֖ה עֲלִיתֶ֣ם עָלֵ֑ינוּ וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ לֶאֱס֤וֹר אֶת־ שִׁמְשׁוֹן֙ עָלִ֔ינוּ לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת ל֔וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר עָ֥שָׂה לָֽנוּ׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mə·rū ’îš yə·hū·ḏāh lā·māh ‘ă·lî·ṯem ‘ā·lê·nū way·yō·mə·rū le·’ĕ·sō·wr ’eṯ- šim·šō·wn ‘ā·lî·nū la·‘ă·śō·wṯ lōw ka·’ă·šer ‘ā·śāh lā·nū
verses.literal: Why have you attacked us said the men of Judah The Philistines replied We have come to arrest Samson and pay him back for what he has done to us
verses.literalPt: E perguntaram-lhes os homens de Judá: Por que subistes contra nós? E eles responderam: Subimos para amarrar a Sansão, para lhe fazer a ele como ele nos fez a nós.

verses.original: וַיֵּרְד֡וּ שְׁלֹשֶׁת֩ אֲלָפִ֨ים אִ֜ישׁ מִֽיהוּדָ֗ה אֶל־ סְעִיף֮ סֶ֣לַע עֵיטָם֒ וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ לְשִׁמְשׁ֗וֹן הֲלֹ֤א יָדַ֙עְתָּ֙ כִּֽי־ מֹשְׁלִ֥ים בָּ֙נוּ֙ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וּמַה־ זֹּ֖את עָשִׂ֣יתָ לָּ֑נוּ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֔ם כַּאֲשֶׁר֙ עָ֣שׂוּ לִ֔י כֵּ֖ן עָשִׂ֥יתִי לָהֶֽם׃
verses.transliteration: way·yê·rə·ḏū šə·lō·šeṯ ’ă·lā·p̄îm ’îš mî·hū·ḏāh ’el- sə·‘îp̄ se·la‘ ‘ê·ṭām way·yō·mə·rū lə·šim·šō·wn hă·lō yā·ḏa‘·tā kî- mō·šə·lîm bā·nū pə·liš·tîm ū·mah- zōṯ ‘ā·śî·ṯā lā·nū way·yō·mer lā·hem ka·’ă·šer ‘ā·śū lî kên ‘ā·śî·ṯî lā·hem
verses.literal: In response, three thousand men of Judah went to the cave at the rock of Etam and they asked Samson Do you not realize that the Philistines rule over us What . . . have you done to us I have done to them what they did to me he replied
verses.literalPt: Então três mil homens de Judá desceram até a fenda da rocha de Etã, e disseram a Sansão: Não sabias tu que os filisteus dominam sobre nós? Por que, pois, nos fizeste isto? E ele lhes disse: Assim como eles me fizeram a mim, eu lhes fiz a eles.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֤אמְרוּ לוֹ֙ לֶאֱסָרְךָ֣ יָרַ֔דְנוּ לְתִתְּךָ֖ בְּיַד־ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ שִׁמְשׁ֔וֹן הִשָּׁבְע֣וּ לִ֔י פֶּֽן־ תִּפְגְּע֥וּן בִּ֖י אַתֶּֽם׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mə·rū lōw le·’ĕ·sā·rə·ḵā yā·raḏ·nū lə·ṯit·tə·ḵā bə·yaḏ- pə·liš·tîm way·yō·mer lā·hem šim·šō·wn hiš·šā·ḇə·‘ū lî pen- tip̄·gə·‘ūn bî ’at·tem
verses.literal: But they said to him We have come down to arrest you and hand you over to . . . the Philistines Samson replied Swear to me that you will not kill me yourselves
verses.literalPt: E disseram-lhe: Descemos para te amarrar e te entregar nas mãos dos filisteus. Então Sansão lhes disse: Jurai-me que vós mesmos não me acometereis.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֧אמְרוּ ל֣וֹ לֵאמֹ֗ר לֹ֚א כִּֽי־ אָסֹ֤ר נֶֽאֱסָרְךָ֙ וּנְתַנּ֣וּךָ בְיָדָ֔ם וְהָמֵ֖ת לֹ֣א נְמִיתֶ֑ךָ וַיַּאַסְרֻ֗הוּ בִּשְׁנַ֙יִם֙ עֲבֹתִ֣ים חֲדָשִׁ֔ים וַֽיַּעֲל֖וּהוּ מִן־ הַסָּֽלַע׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mə·rū lōw lê·mōr lō kî- ’ā·sōr ne·’ĕ·sā·rə·ḵā ū·nə·ṯan·nū·ḵā ḇə·yā·ḏām wə·hā·mêṯ lō nə·mî·ṯe·ḵā way·ya·’as·ru·hū biš·na·yim ‘ă·ḇō·ṯîm ḥă·ḏā·šîm way·ya·‘ă·lū·hū min- has·sā·la‘
verses.literal: No they answered we will not . . . kill you but we will tie you up securely . . . and hand you over to them So they bound him with two new ropes and led him up from the rock
verses.literalPt: E eles lhe falaram, dizendo: Não, mas fortemente te amarraremos, e te entregaremos nas mãos deles; porém de maneira nenhuma te mataremos. E amarraram-no com duas cordas novas e fizeram-no subir da rocha.

verses.original: הוּא־ בָ֣א עַד־ לֶ֔חִי וּפִלְשִׁתִּ֖ים הֵרִ֣יעוּ לִקְרָאת֑וֹ וַתִּצְלַ֨ח עָלָ֜יו ר֣וּחַ יְהוָ֗ה וַתִּהְיֶ֨ינָה הָעֲבֹתִ֜ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־ זְרוֹעוֹתָ֗יו כַּפִּשְׁתִּים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּעֲר֣וּ בָאֵ֔שׁ וַיִּמַּ֥סּוּ אֱסוּרָ֖יו מֵעַ֥ל יָדָֽיו׃
verses.transliteration: hū- ḇā ‘aḏ- le·ḥî ū·p̄il·šit·tīm hê·rî·‘ū liq·rā·ṯōw wat·tiṣ·laḥ ‘ā·lāw rū·aḥ Yah·weh wat·tih·ye·nāh hā·‘ă·ḇō·ṯîm ’ă·šer ‘al- zə·rō·w·‘ō·w·ṯāw kap·piš·tîm ’ă·šer bā·‘ă·rū ḇā·’êš way·yim·mas·sū ’ĕ·sū·rāw mê·‘al yā·ḏāw
verses.literal: When Samson arrived in Lehi the Philistines came out shouting against him And the Spirit of the LORD came mightily upon him The ropes on his arms became like burnt . . . flax and the bonds broke loose from his hands
verses.literalPt: E, vindo ele a Leí, os filisteus lhe saíram ao encontro, jubilando; porém o Espírito do SENHOR poderosamente se apossou dele, e as cordas que ele tinha nos braços se tornaram como fios de linho que se queimaram no fogo, e as suas amarraduras se desfizeram das suas mãos.

verses.original: וַיִּמְצָ֥א לְחִֽי־ חֲמ֖וֹר טְרִיָּ֑ה וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יָדוֹ֙ וַיִּקָּחֶ֔הָ וַיַּךְ־ בָּ֖הּ אֶ֥לֶף אִֽישׁ׃
verses.transliteration: way·yim·ṣā lə·ḥî- ḥă·mō·wr ṭə·rî·yāh way·yiš·laḥ yā·ḏōw way·yiq·qā·ḥe·hā way·yaḵ- bāh ’e·lep̄ ’îš
verses.literal: He found the fresh jawbone of a donkey reached out his hand and took it and struck down a thousand men
verses.literalPt: E achou uma queixada fresca de um jumento, e estendeu a sua mão, e tomou-a, e feriu com ela mil homens.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שִׁמְשׁ֔וֹן בִּלְחִ֣י הַחֲמ֔וֹר חֲמ֖וֹר חֲמֹרָתָ֑יִם בִּלְחִ֣י הַחֲמ֔וֹר הִכֵּ֖יתִי אֶ֥לֶף אִֽישׁ׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer šim·šō·wn bil·ḥî ha·ḥă·mō·wr ḥă·mō·wr ḥă·mō·rā·ṯā·yim bil·ḥî ha·ḥă·mō·wr hik·kê·ṯî ’e·lep̄ ’îš
verses.literal: Then Samson said With the jawbone of a donkey I have piled them into heaps With the jawbone of a donkey I have slain a thousand men
verses.literalPt: Então disse Sansão: Com uma queixada de jumento, montões sobre montões; com uma queixada de jumento feri a mil homens.

verses.original: וַֽיְהִי֙ כְּכַלֹּת֣וֹ לְדַבֵּ֔ר וַיַּשְׁלֵ֥ךְ הַלְּחִ֖י מִיָּד֑וֹ וַיִּקְרָ֛א לַמָּק֥וֹם הַה֖וּא רָ֥מַת לֶֽחִי׃
verses.transliteration: way·hî kə·ḵal·lō·ṯōw lə·ḏab·bêr way·yaš·lêḵ hal·lə·ḥî mî·yā·ḏōw way·yiq·rā lam·mā·qō·wm ha·hū rā·maṯ le·ḥî
verses.literal: And when Samson had finished speaking he cast the jawbone from his hand and he named that place Ramath-lehi
verses.literalPt: E aconteceu que, acabando ele de falar, lançou a queixada da sua mão; e chamou aquele lugar Ramate-Leí.

verses.original: וַיִּצְמָא֮ מְאֹד֒ וַיִּקְרָ֤א אֶל־ יְהוָה֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר אַתָּה֙ נָתַ֣תָּ בְיַֽד־ עַבְדְּךָ֔ אֶת־ הַתְּשׁוּעָ֥ה הַגְּדֹלָ֖ה הַזֹּ֑את וְעַתָּה֙ אָמ֣וּת בַּצָּמָ֔א וְנָפַלְתִּ֖י בְּיַ֥ד הָעֲרֵלִֽים׃
verses.transliteration: way·yiṣ·mā mə·’ōḏ way·yiq·rā ’el- Yah·weh way·yō·mar ’at·tāh nā·ṯa·tā ḇə·yaḏ- ‘aḇ·də·ḵā ’eṯ- hat·tə·šū·‘āh hag·gə·ḏō·lāh haz·zōṯ wə·‘at·tāh ’ā·mūṯ baṣ·ṣā·mā wə·nā·p̄al·tî bə·yaḏ hā·‘ă·rê·lîm
verses.literal: And being very thirsty Samson cried out to the LORD . . . You have accomplished this great deliverance through Your servant Must I now die of thirst and fall into the hands of the uncircumcised
verses.literalPt: E como tivesse grande sede, clamou ao SENHOR, e disse: Pela mão do teu servo tu deste esta grande salvação; morrerei eu pois agora de sede, e cairei na mão destes incircuncisos?

verses.original: וַיִּבְקַ֨ע אֱלֹהִ֜ים אֶת־ הַמַּכְתֵּ֣שׁ אֲשֶׁר־ בַּלֶּ֗חִי וַיֵּצְא֨וּ מִמֶּ֤נּוּ מַ֙יִם֙ וַיֵּ֔שְׁתְּ וַתָּ֥שָׁב רוּח֖וֹ וַיֶּ֑חִי עַל־ כֵּ֣ן׀ קָרָ֣א שְׁמָ֗הּ עֵ֤ין הַקּוֹרֵא֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּלֶּ֔חִי עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃
verses.transliteration: way·yiḇ·qa‘ ’ĕ·lō·hîm ’eṯ- ham·maḵ·têš ’ă·šer- bal·le·ḥî way·yê·ṣə·’ū mim·men·nū ma·yim way·yê·šət wat·tā·šāḇ rū·ḥōw way·ye·ḥî ‘al- kên qā·rā šə·māh ‘ên haq·qō·w·rê ’ă·šer bal·le·ḥî ‘aḏ hay·yō·wm haz·zeh
verses.literal: So God opened up the hollow place in Lehi and water came out of it When Samson drank his strength returned and he was revived That is why . . . he named it . . . En-hakkore and it remains in Lehi to this day
verses.literalPt: Então Deus fendeu uma cavidade que estava na queixada; e saiu dela água, e bebeu; e recobrou o seu espírito e reanimou-se; por isso chamou aquele lugar: A fonte do que clama, que está em Leí até ao dia de hoje.

verses.original: וַיִּשְׁפֹּ֧ט אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל בִּימֵ֥י פְלִשְׁתִּ֖ים עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָֽה׃פ
verses.transliteration: way·yiš·pōṭ ’eṯ- yiś·rā·’êl bî·mê p̄ə·liš·tîm ‘eś·rîm šā·nāh
verses.literal: And Samson judged Israel for twenty years in the days of the Philistines
verses.literalPt: E julgou a Israel, nos dias dos filisteus, vinte anos.
